# Rules engine provenance

Source: user's `dnd-rpg-cli-mcp` repository, committed snapshot `905beabe71de91f3b1af0b30ba284d942787352b`.

Only `src/core/` and its MIT license were imported with `git archive`. Uncommitted edits, credentials, saves, browser/CLI providers and application assets were not imported. This snapshot is independent of the adjacent checkout.

Application-specific world, quest, dialogue and memory logic stays in the adapter. `entry.ts` and `scripts/build-rules.js` compile the source into an ESM module; built output is not committed.

One storage fix is applied in the snapshot: `state/store.ts` writes the SQLite export to a temporary file and renames it, avoiding a partially overwritten database after interruption.
Trailing spaces in four upstream TypeScript files have also been normalized; no rules logic was changed by that formatting step.

Two rules corrections are applied locally: level-one armor class is calculated from the final racial ability scores and equipped armor, and combat completion records an explicit victory/retreat/defeat outcome. The adapter awards victory objectives only for an actual victory. Inventory-use and armor-class helpers are exported so the UI uses the same authoritative rules.

The adapter also imports the existing effective-armor and removed-effect condition cleanup helpers. The cleanup helper was exported without changing its rules behavior, so elapsed exploration time removes an effect and its associated condition consistently with combat expiration.

The main adventure opts into explicit player turn completion with `ui_player_turn_control`: spending an action preserves the living player's remaining bonus action/movement until End Turn. Other callers retain the snapshot's automatic behavior. Typed inventory defense/attack/save bonuses can also be prepared outside combat, using the same consumption and duration fields; combat effects are mirrored into the party sheet. The adapter routes combat inventory use through the existing action-cost resolver. XP thresholds and inventory merging are exported for progression UI and durable loot.

The economy adapter imports the existing pure long-rest and state ability-check helpers (including bonus consumption and roll-log construction) through `entry.ts`; these exports do not modify their rules behavior. Market finances, stock, services and the optional comfortable-rest bonus are application mechanics in `src/adventure-economy.js`.

The adapter additionally exports existing incapacitation and reaction-spending helpers for original casting and accurate UI action costs. This changes no upstream helper behavior. Catalog combat casts in the application now use the existing chooseAction path rather than the direct castSpell resolver; original spells synchronize spent slot resources into combatants before normal party synchronization.

## SRD attribution

The exact-order follow-up adds a one-shot registered-NPC cast directive, a pure prospective-turn option view and saved outcome flags. SceneRunner and generated opening paths preserve just the two order/result overlays without overwriting script/adventure/snapshot state. Exports of existing buildTurnView, createTurnBudget and the ordinary spell turn resolver support previews/tests. The existing area target helper is exported and defaults to allies-inclusive selection for Sleep/Color Spray only; other area behavior is unchanged. Positive-HP healing now preserves unconscious condition/effect sources, while0-to-positive revival retains its medical cleanup. These are local rules corrections; full tabletop area geometry is not implemented.

The companion-combat adapter adds five preferences only for explicitly registered NPC allies. The existing legal weapon/item/casting paths execute their next actual turns, consume ammunition or finite healing items, and preserve action costs. Preferences never control human players. The adapter also exports the existing availableAutomatedSrdSpells helper without changing it. Party possession/gear transfer logic remains original application code outside the imported snapshot.

The medical follow-up corrects shared applyHealing, catalog healTarget, inventory healing and combat-to-character life synchronization: both death markers prohibit ordinary healing, ineffective healing cannot clear life conditions, actual healing resets old failed saves, and cache synchronization does not restore them. Shared progression preserves0 currentHP and prevents fresh spendable resources for corpses during level-up. Existing death-save, stabilization, item-charge and feature helpers are exported; medical clocks, recipient/owner separation and shared rest timing remain adapter code in src/adventure-medicine.js, src/adventure-first-aid.js and src/adventure-rest.js.

The application now opts registered NPC allies into `narrative/companion-combat-ai.ts`, an independently written finite controller using existing spell, action, death-save and reaction resolvers. Generated encounter startup and SceneRunner automatic turns call its hooks; `rules/combat.ts` exposes an optional automatic death-save hook, retaining manual behavior for other callers. `consequence-engine.ts` captures at most twelve recent actual combat logs and dead NPC resource snapshots only when companion registration is present, before terminal combat deletion. No external model is called by these hooks. Existing character-build/level/slot helpers are exported for same-ID persistence and tested spell foundations.

The original-spell follow-up adds independently written `homebrew/original-spell-spec.cjs` and `actions/original-spell-actions.ts`, moving the app's existing schema/power model into a shared validator/interpreter. The companion hook accepts one bounded owned original definition and calls the same runtime with its existing RNG. The readied Counterspell helper has optional validated-definition metadata for original spell level; unknown bare IDs gain no level. The two service flag merges also preserve the existing generated leveled-spell marker. ESM bundling supplies Node createRequire for the shared CJS validator's existing external zod dependency. NPC books and workshop UI remain original adapter code.

The SRD text has been represented as executable rules and structured game content. Original compatible content and application code remain under their respective MIT licenses. This project is unofficial and does not include an endorsement by Wizards of the Coast.

The environment adapter additionally exports the existing resolveAttack, characterToCombatant, setCombatDistanceBand, spendObjectInteraction and isCharmedBySource helpers without changing their upstream behavior. Lazy props, finite anchors and persistent adapter NPC bodies are original application code in src/environment-interactions.js; the independently written dialogue queue does not import OpenMAIC AGPL code.

Persistent NPC battles use exports of existing startCombat, runAutomaticTurns, hasPendingDeathSaves and focusNextDeathSaveTurn. One narrow local correction in consequence-engine.ts syncPartyFromCombat captures at most six exact enemy bodies into a JSON flag only for environment IDs beginning npc_encounter:. This lets the adapter retain terminal damage/conditions before normal core completion deletes combat; ordinary encounters keep their existing behavior. Original bounded role profiles are application code in src/npc-encounters.js, not additional official SRD stat blocks.

The spell-turn follow-up extends the existing TurnBudget with actual casting history and pure eligibility/spend helpers. Catalog/original resolvers, Quickened/Sorcery Point costs, own/off-turn reactions, direct service routing and native option previews share this rule. Core readied metadata uses the selected spell slot for Counterspell; anchored actual legacy cantrips do not authorize arbitrary IDs. Save parsing migrates exact matching old authored markers, preserving ambiguous costs explicitly. The independently written NPC controller adds a bounded owned original-book planner and uses existing effect/RNG/expiry helpers without model calls. General Ready-spell preparation remains refused/unsupported. See SPELL_TURN_ECONOMY.md for sources and tests.

The weapon-possession correction extends the existing shared equipment guard to ordinary catalog and modeled/generated weapons: a real owned, equipped instance is required before rolls or costs, and existing option builders use that same guard. Spell attacks, unarmed strikes and noncatalog NPC profile attacks retain their existing paths. New standard cleric foundations use the existing simple mace inventory/equipment model; their unsourced longsword fallback is removed. Starting equipment options no longer retain unrelated catalog weapon attacks from a different class kit. Existing campaigns receive no free weapon or restock during loading. These local corrections are covered by native/controller weapon-ownership regressions.
